name: Tapo L530E (EU)

matter.note: No official source states Matter either way: the EU spec page lists only Alexa and Google, and we found no CSA listing for the L530E. TP-Link's Matter colour bulb is the L535E. Not confirmed.

apple_home.note: The EU spec page lists only Alexa and Google, but no official source says Apple Home is unsupported, and TP-Link's US bulb listing tags the L530E as HomeKit-supported. Not confirmed.

google_home.note: Through the Tapo cloud integration for Google Home.

smartthings.note: Via TP-Link account linking in the SmartThings app (Partner devices > Tapo). TP-Link's SmartThings FAQ lists the L530E; the user guide names SmartThings too. Basic controls only. The FAQ cited is the US edition.

home_assistant.note: Listed as supported by the official TP-Link Smart Home integration; needs TP-Link cloud credentials and may need Third-Party Compatibility enabled in the Tapo app.

hubRequired.note: Connects straight to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and is controlled from the Tapo app; no bridge needed.

localControl.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link integration talks to the bulb on the local network without the TP-Link cloud, though it uses your TP-Link account credentials to authenticate.

colorType.note: 16 million colours plus tunable white, 2500–6500 K.

lumens.note: 806 lm, comparable to a 60 W incandescent.

bulbBase.note: E27 for the EU/TW version; the US version is E26.

summary: The Tapo L530E (EU) works with Alexa and Google Home through TP-Link's cloud skill and integration, and with SmartThings once you link your TP-Link account. No hub: it joins 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi directly, and Home Assistant's official TP-Link Smart Home integration controls it on the local network. Expect 806 lumens, 16 million colours and tunable white from 2500 to 6500 K, on an E27 base. Apple Home and Matter are both unconfirmed, since the EU spec page lists only Alexa and Google.
caveats: Apple Home and Matter support aren't confirmed; TP-Link's Matter colour bulb is the Tapo L535E, not this one.
Home Assistant needs your TP-Link account credentials, and you may have to turn on Third-Party Compatibility in the Tapo app.
This is the E27 EU version; the US version uses an E26 base.
